msg: Google Fonts is pulled from a US host, so the visitor's IP is transferred before the page paints. LG Munchen I, 20 O 14144/19 (2022-01-20) awarded EUR 100 damages to one visitor for exactly this. Fix: download the .woff2 next to your docs and serve it yourself.

constants.law: GDPR Art. 44-49 (transfers to a third country) + Art. 6(1) (no legal basis for the IP disclosure)
constants.ruling: LG Munchen I, 20 O 14144/19, 2022-01-20, EUR 100 per visitor
constants.eea_note: EEA = EU 27 + Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway. The US has an adequacy decision (EU-US Data Privacy Framework, 2023-07-10) but only for certified recipients; a CDN edge is not certified for you by default.
constants.scope: asset URLs inside .md, .mdx and .html docs; fenced code blocks are treated as examples and skipped

msg: A Gravatar avatar is loaded from Automattic in the US. The request carries the reader's IP plus the MD5 of an author e-mail. Fix: commit the avatar image into the repo and point at the local path.

This screenshot is hotlinked from Imgur (US). Every reader of the page is announced to Imgur, and Imgur may delete or replace the file without telling you. Fix: move the image into docs/img/ and reference it relatively.
This image sits on SM.MS (China). China has no EU adequacy decision, so this is an Art. 44 transfer with no safeguard on file. Fix: re-upload to a host inside the EEA or into the repo itself.

constants.no_adequacy: China, Russia and India have no EU adequacy decision as of 2026-09-21; an SCC set plus a transfer impact assessment would be required.

msg: Free image hosts ImgBB / PostImage are US-run and give you no data processing agreement at all. Fix: host the file yourself; these links also rot once the free bucket is recycled.

The asset is served by GitHub in the US. Fine inside GitHub, but on your own published docs page it is an uncontrolled third-country transfer. Fix: copy the file into the site build instead of hotlinking it.

jsDelivr resolves to US and Chinese edge nodes depending on the reader, so you cannot name the receiving country in your Art. 30 record. Fix: install the package and bundle it, or self-host the single file.
unpkg.com is a US CDN in front of npm. Loading a script from it hands the reader's IP and referrer to a party you have no contract with. Fix: vendor the file into your assets folder.
cdnjs is operated by Cloudflare (US). Subresource integrity does not help here: the transfer happens with the request, not with the payload. Fix: serve the library from your own origin.

A Chinese object-storage bucket is serving this asset. Typical when an editor upload plugin was left on its default backend. Fix: repoint the upload backend at an EEA bucket and rewrite the published links.
A plain YouTube embed sets cookies and profiles the reader on load. Fix: use youtube-nocookie.com behind a click-to-load placeholder, so nothing leaves until the reader asks for the video.
Analytics fires on page load, before any consent choice exists on a docs page. Fix: gate it behind consent, or use a self-hosted counter that stores no identifier.
Build badges are live images: each reader pings the badge host. Harmless in a repo, a transfer on a published page. Fix: commit the rendered .svg and refresh it in CI.
Adobe Fonts is loaded from a US host for every reader, the same pattern the Munich Google Fonts ruling punished. Fix: switch to a licensed self-hosted webfont file.
A comment widget loads third-party script and, for Disqus, tracking cookies before a word is typed. Fix: load it only after an explicit click, and name the processor in your privacy notice.

constants.art30: Art. 30(1)(e) asks you to record transfers to third countries and the safeguards used; a widget you never listed cannot be recorded.

msg: The diagram source is encoded into the URL, so your internal architecture is sent to a render service along with the reader's IP. Fix: render the diagram at build time and commit the .svg.
This asset is fetched over plain http, so the transfer is also readable in transit. Fix: use https, or a relative path if the file lives with the docs.
